true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Second downsize definition overwrites the width/height API

Ruby does not overload methods, so `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` replaces the method defined four lines above that takes max_width and max_height. Any existing caller that passes numeric width and height (the previous public signature) now treats the width as the geometry string and the height as `opts`. `opts[:allow_animation]` then raises, and even a rescued failure returns false so thumbnails and other downsizes stop being generated. Keep a single method that accepts either a geometry string or two integers.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client size check hardcodes 10MB for every upload type

`validateUploadedFile` used to read `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, so images and attachments each followed their site setting. It now always uses `10 * 1024`. Attachments are no longer limited by `max_attachment_size_kb`, and an admin who raised `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB will have the client reject files the server would accept. The 413 handler at the same file was also changed from `max_image_size_kb` to 10MB, so the error text no longer matches the configured or proxy limit. Only relax the client cap for images that the server will downsize, and keep the attachment setting.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Percentage geometry is invalid for the animated downsize path

When the upload is a GIF and `SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails` is on, `optimize` switches to gifsicle instructions (`--resize-fit` plus the dimensions argument). Those instructions expect a WIDTHxHEIGHT, but the new caller passes `"80%"`. gifsicle then fails, `downsize` returns false, and the loop ignores that return value and retries the same file five times. Animated uploads are never reduced and still hit the size check. The non-animated instruction also appends `\>` , so the geometry becomes `80%\>` rather than a plain percentage. Use a WxH target (or a percentage only on the convert path) and stop the loop when downsize returns false.

true_positives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Downsize reads and writes the same tempfile path

The new loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)`. ImageMagick `convert` cannot reliably use one path as both input and output: it often truncates or replaces the file before the source is fully read, producing an empty or corrupt image. The upload Tempfile is already open, so a convert that writes via a new inode leaves that FD on the original bytes while `tempfile.size` and `Upload.create_for` still use the open file. Downsizing then either no-ops or stores the undownsized (or empty) image. Write to a separate temp path, replace the upload file only after success, and reopen/re-stat before `create_for`.

false_positives.candidate:
No coverage for automatic downsize-on-upload

The new upload path (five 80% passes, same-path convert, GIF vs still image, and what happens when the file is still over `max_image_size_kb`) has no tests in this change. A failure of convert, a stale Tempfile size, or an attachment accidentally included in the 10MB cap would ship unnoticed. Add controller or model tests for a still image that shrinks under the setting, a GIF with animation allowed, a downsize that returns false, and a non-image that must still obey the attachment limit.

URL fetches always allow 10MB, including non-images

API uploads that pass a URL used to download at most `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`. The cap is now a fixed `10.megabytes` for every type, and the later downsize block only runs when `FileHelper.is_image?(filename)` is true. Non-image URL uploads therefore bypass the configured size limit and can pull up to 10MB even when `max_attachment_size_kb` is much smaller. Limit the raised cap to images that will actually be downsized, and keep the site setting for other files.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Nil host raises instead of failing validation

before_validation calls self.host.sub! with no nil guard. create/update pass params[:embeddable_host][:host] straight through, so a missing host raises NoMethodError (500) rather than a validation error from render_json_error. record_for_host also returns false (not nil) when the URI cannot be parsed; TopicEmbed.import then calls eh.try(:category_id) on false, which raises instead of falling back to no category.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Update and destroy 500 when the id is missing

update and destroy load the row with where(id:).first and immediately call save_host or host.destroy. An unknown id leaves host nil, so the action raises NoMethodError instead of a 404. save_host also does not check that category_id refers to a real category, so an admin can persist a dangling category_id and later imports will create topics in a category that does not exist.

true_positives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Allowed-host lookup misses case and port

record_for_host compares lower(host) to URI#host without downcasing the URI host, so a referer or embed URL whose host has any uppercase letters never matches a stored row. It also drops the port, while the host format validation allows :port and before_validation does not strip it. A saved host such as example.com:8080 can never be allowed, because the lookup host is only example.com.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts are not normalized and are interpolated into SQL

Existing embeddable_hosts values are inserted with raw SQL, bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation that strips http(s):// and paths. record_for_host compares URI#host (e.g. eviltrout.com) to the stored string, so previously working entries like "http://eviltrout.com" or "https://example.com/path" no longer match and embedding/referer checks fail after upgrade. The same statement interpolates the host inside single quotes, so a value containing a quote breaks the migration or injects SQL.

true_positives.golden_comment: The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migrated hosts are not normalized and are interpolated into SQL

Existing embeddable_hosts values are inserted with raw SQL, bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation that strips http(s):// and paths. record_for_host compares URI#host (e.g. eviltrout.com) to the stored string, so previously working entries like "http://eviltrout.com" or "https://example.com/path" no longer match and embedding/referer checks fail after upgrade. The same statement interpolates the host inside single quotes, so a value containing a quote breaks the migration or injects SQL.

true_positives.golden_comment: The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Migration crashes when embed_category is unset

The migration always does execute(... embed_category ...)[0]['id'] before checking whether a row exists. embed_category was an optional site setting, so most databases have no site_settings row (or no category whose name matches it). An empty result makes [0] nil and the migration raises NoMethodError, so upgrades that never customized embedding cannot run this migration. The same pattern on the uncategorized_category_id fallback (line 15) crashes if that row is missing.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

false_positives.candidate:
Host regex rejects valid hosts the old setting allowed

validates_format_of requires a dotted hostname whose final label is 2–5 letters. That rejects IP addresses, localhost, and real TLDs longer than 5 characters (for example .museum or .cloud). Those values could be stored in the old embeddable_hosts setting and are inserted by the migration without validation, but they cannot be saved or edited through the new admin API.

Plural id hydration assumes a non-null array

The new *_ids branch always calls obj[k].map. Any rest-serialized payload that includes a plural foreign key as null (rather than []) now throws while hydrating, which breaks find/findAll for that type. Previously only singular *_id keys were handled, and only when a match was found.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsubscribe crashes when no TopicUser row exists

TopicsController#unsubscribe loads the user's TopicUser with find_by and immediately reads tu.notification_level. If the recipient has never had a topic_users row (or it was deleted), tu is nil and the action raises NoMethodError instead of unsubscribing. The email link is therefore a 500 for that user, and no muted/regular level is stored. Create the row (TopicUser.change) or no-op safely when it is missing.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
Level change skips TopicUser.change and does not actually stop watching

The action assigns notification_level and calls save! instead of TopicUser.change. That skips notifications_reason_id and notifications_changed_at. auto_track and update_last_read only keep a user-chosen level when notifications_reason_id is set; with it left nil, the next visit or auto-track promotes the user back to tracking, so the unsubscribe does not stick. Separately, watching/tracking (level > regular) is only lowered to regular, not muted, while regular is muted. Watching users still receive reply, mention, and quote mail, which contradicts the new email copy that this link stops notifications for the topic. A second GET then takes the else branch and mutes them, so refresh or a double click changes the level again.

No specs for the unsubscribe action

The only test change passes unsubscribe_url into MessageBuilder and still only asserts that the preferences URL appears. Nothing covers TopicsController#unsubscribe: missing TopicUser, watching vs regular vs muted outcomes, notifications_reason_id being set, idempotent repeats, or the email string interpolating unsubscribe_url. Those paths are where this feature breaks, so the PR can merge with the action crashing or not sticking.

Topic unsubscribe is an unauthenticated-token GET that mutates state

t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and t/:topic_id/unsubscribe are GET routes with no per-user unsubscribe key, and TopicsController#unsubscribe writes notification_level as a side effect. Rails CSRF protection does not cover GET, so any site can mute or downgrade a logged-in victim for a known topic id with an img or prefetch of that URL. Mail-gateway link scanners that follow the link in an already logged-in browser do the same. One-click email unsubscribe needs a POST or a secret, user-specific token, and must not depend on an existing session cookie.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Block match stats are rolled back or double-counted

BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count and calls save while EmailValidator is running inside User validation. UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, so the counter is updated twice. user.save wraps validations in a transaction, and when the email is rejected that transaction rolls back the BlockedEmail write. With call_discourse_hub off, a real blocked signup therefore leaves match_count and last_match_at unchanged; with it on, only the outer valid? write sticks. The model specs call should_block? directly, so they never see this and the block statistics are wrong in production.

true_positives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Domain whitelist/blacklist regex is unanchored

email_in_restriction_setting? builds Regexp.new("@(#{domains})") after only escaping dots, with no end anchor and no escape of other metacharacters. A whitelist entry gmail.com therefore matches user@gmail.com.evil.test (and any longer suffix), so the signup is treated as allowed. A blacklist entry can also false-positive on addresses that merely contain that domain string after @. This is the only domain check on User now that email_validator was removed, and the new spec stubs should_block? and never covers it.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email lookup is an exact, case-sensitive match

should_block? looks up BlockedEmail.where(email: email) with the raw address and no downcase or strip. Postgres unique/equality on string is case-sensitive, and nothing in User.new_from_params or EmailValidator normalizes the address before this check. A row for bad@spam.com will not match Bad@spam.com or " bad@spam.com ", so a blocked address can still register by changing case or adding whitespace. The unique index has the same problem, so both casings can be stored as separate rows.

true_positives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Remote fetch follows redirects off the embeddable host

`TopicRetriever` only checks that `URI(embed_url).host` equals `embeddable_host`, then `TopicEmbed.import_remote` calls `open(url).read`. open-uri follows redirects by default, so a page on the allowed host (or a query-string URL an attacker can get that host to serve) can 302 to an internal address (`http://127.0.0.1`, cloud metadata, etc.). The Sidekiq worker will request that target and import the body as a topic. Disable redirects or re-check the host after each hop, and do the same for `PollFeed`'s `open(feed_polling_url)`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Resize message origin check is inverted and too loose

`discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts the message whenever `e.origin` is any substring of `discourseUrl`, including the empty string (sandboxed/data iframes, where `origin` is `""` and `indexOf` returns 0). It does not require `e.origin` to equal the Discourse origin. Any such frame can set the embed iframe height. Compare parsed origins for equality instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
postMessage targetOrigin is a full referer URL

`parent.postMessage(..., '<%= request.referer %>')` passes the full referring page URL. `postMessage`'s targetOrigin must be an origin (`scheme://host[:port]`). A path-bearing referer does not match the parent origin, so browsers drop the message (or throw) and the parent iframe never receives `discourse-resize`. Height will stay at the default and the embed will clip. Pass only the referer origin.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Embed URL is interpolated into HTML unescaped The imported-from footer builds `#{url}` and then stores the string as raw HTML. The only check is `/^https?:\/\//`, so a URL such as `http://host/' onclick='alert(1)` or one containing `<` breaks out of the attribute/text and becomes stored XSS in the post and the embed iframe. Escape the URL for both the href attribute and the link text.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Embed template has invalid ERB (`end if`)

`<%- end if %>` compiles to the Ruby statement `end if`, which is a syntax error. Rendering `/embed/best` after a topic exists will raise ActionView::Template::Error instead of showing the discussion. It must be `<% end %>`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Feed poll crashes when an item has no content

`CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` assumes every RSS/Atom item has a non-nil `content` string. SimpleRSS items often only set `description` (or neither). The first such item raises NoMethodError, aborts the rest of the feed, and — with `retry: false` — drops the hourly import until the next run. Nil-check and fall back to `description` before unescaping.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Disqus import now depends on a live HTTP fetch

The importer used to create the topic from the XML export. It now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote`, which `open`s `t[:link]` with no rescue. A dead, redirected, or non-HTML link raises and aborts the whole XML import; even a soft failure (`post` blank) silently skips every comment on that thread. Network errors need to be isolated per thread, with a fallback topic so comments are not dropped.

Every embed miss enqueues a fetch with no host or dedupe check

`best` enqueues `retrieve_topic` for any `embed_url` as soon as no `TopicEmbed` row exists. It never checks that the URL's host is `embeddable_host` (that check is only inside the job) and does not dedupe. A page on the allowed host, or repeated views while the topic is still missing, fills the queue; if `embed_by_username` is blank or the fetch fails, nothing is created and `loading.html.erb` reloads every 30s forever. Validate the host before enqueue and avoid enqueueing when a recent attempt already failed.

raw_html cook path stores and serves unsanitized HTML

`Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged when `cook_method` is `raw_html`, skipping the normal Sanitize/PrettyText pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` writes RSS item HTML (and Readability output) with that cook method, and `embed/best.html.erb` prints it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. The same cooked HTML is what the main topic page serves. An RSS item can therefore inject script or event-handler markup into every viewer of the imported topic. RSS bodies need the same tag/attribute allowlist (and `javascript:` URL rejection) as the rest of post cooking before they are stored.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order() mixin is off-by-one for 2009 flexbox

@mixin order writes the same $val to -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group as to the modern order property. Those 2009 properties are 1-based (the initial value is 1), while order is 0-based (initial value 0). Autoprefixer and the usual Discourse mixin emit $val + 1 for the ordinal-group properties. As written, order(1) is a no-op in old WebKit (same as the default group), and order(0) or a negative order cannot be represented. Header .panel uses order(3) and .extra-info-wrapper uses order(2); those still sort after untouched siblings only by accident. Fix the two box-ordinal-group lines to $val + 1 so the prefixed output matches order.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

false_positives.candidate:
Docked topic title can push header controls off-screen

.extra-info-wrapper is now a flex item of .d-header .contents (order 2) but never sets min-width: 0, flex-shrink, or overflow. Flex items default to min-width: auto, so a long topic title's min-content width cannot shrink. margin-left: auto on .panel then cannot keep the header icons in view: the row overflows and the panel is pushed past the viewport. The old float layout did not have this min-content floor. Give the wrapper flex: 1 1 auto; min-width: 0; overflow: hidden (and ellipsis on the title) so the title truncates and the panel stays on screen.

Small-action description no longer fills the row

.small-action is now a flex row, but .small-action-desc stays at the default flex: 0 1 auto and only has padding: 0 1.5%, replacing the old block padding (0.5em 0 0.5em 4em) that made the description full width beside the floated avatar. A flex item sizes to its content, so the button rule float: right (line 306) only floats inside that shrink-wrapped box, not to the right edge of the action row. Delete/expand controls that used to sit on the far right will sit immediately after the action text. Set flex: 1 1 auto and min-width: 0 on .small-action-desc (or margin-left: auto on the button if it is a flex item).

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
website_name bypasses TL0 website hiding

include_website_name is missing the trailing ? that ActiveModel::Serializers uses (every other include hook in this file is include_*?), so the method is never called and website_name is always serialized. website_name is also absent from untrusted_attributes, which is what hides website, bio, and location for trust-level 0 users viewed anonymously. The profile template now renders model.website_name, so an anonymous visitor still sees a new user's site host and path even though website itself is omitted. That undoes the anti-spam/privacy gate. Add website_name to untrusted_attributes (which defines include_website_name?) and drop the dead include_website_name method; the serializer spec never covers a TL0 user who has a website.

false_positives.candidate:
Same-site host check is case-sensitive and www-asymmetric

website_host is compared to Discourse.current_hostname with == and ends_with? without downcasing. Ruby's URI does not lowercase the host, so http://Example.com/user on an example.com forum fails every branch and website_name is only Example.com, not Example.com/user. The same gap hits the common www vs apex pair: www.example.com (3 labels) vs example.com (2 labels) skips the equal-length sibling branch, and example.com.ends_with?('.www.example.com') is false, so the path is dropped. The reverse (forum on www, website on the apex) does show the path via ends_with?, so the feature is inconsistent for the same site. Normalize both hosts (downcase, and treat a single leading www label as equivalent) before comparing, and cover those cases in the serializer spec.

true_positives.golden_comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Embedded-post username color lightness swapped

The embedded post username link was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so the light-theme branch is no longer 30% and the dark branch is the inverse of the usual 100-minus mapping. Every other conversion in this PR keeps the original lightness on `$primary` and puts `100 - N` on `$secondary`. Light themes will render these names much paler (weaker contrast); dark themes will not get the intended muted secondary color.

true_positives.golden_comment: This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Group member name color flattened to 50%

`.group-member-info .name` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` and is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The adjacent `.title` rule was already 50% and was converted correctly; the name rule was overwritten with that same 50/50 pair instead of `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. Light-theme group member names become lighter than before and no longer differ from titles.

true_positives.golden_comment: In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Mobile flag length hint color inverted

`.custom-message-length` was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. It is now `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The desktop counterpart in this same PR correctly keeps 70% on `$primary` and uses 30% on `$secondary`. On mobile light themes the hint becomes much darker than before; on dark themes it is lightened far more than the desktop rule, so the two layouts no longer match and contrast with the modal background changes.

true_positives.golden_comment: The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.

Embedded-post username color lightness swapped

The embedded post username link was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The replacement is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, so the light-theme branch is no longer 30% and the dark branch is the inverse of the usual 100-minus mapping. true_positives.matched_candidate:

members used to render a JSON array of GroupUserSerializer objects. It now returns {members, meta: {total, limit, offset}}. limit is (params[:limit] || 50).to_i with no upper bound, and offset is not clamped to >= 0. This action is public (only ensure_can_see!). false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

false_positives.candidate:
Fallback locale files are not loaded on translate

The on-demand loader in I18n.translate only calls load_locale for config.locale. FallbackLocaleList and I18n::Backend::Fallbacks then look up SiteSetting.default_locale and :en, but those YAML files stay unloaded unless something else has called ensure_loaded!. The only call site is ApplicationController#set_locale, so jobs, mailers, models, middleware, and I18n.with_locale blocks never load the fallback chain. Missing keys then raise or return the Rails "translation missing" string instead of the site-locale or English string. Because translate also LRU-caches that result (and the production exception handler returns a string rather than raising), a miss can stick in the cache even after the fallback files are loaded later in the same process.

No tests for fallback order or locale loading

The new FallbackLocaleList (user locale, then SiteSetting.default_locale, then :en) and the ensure_loaded! hook are untested. Nothing asserts that a key missing in the user locale resolves to the site locale before English, that string/symbol locales collapse, or that a translation outside ApplicationController#set_locale still loads fallback YAML. Those are the paths this change is most likely to get wrong, and a regression would ship user-visible missing or wrong strings.

Translation cache ignores the fallback chain

The LRU key is only "#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}". With fallbacks enabled, the cached string can come from SiteSetting.default_locale or :en, but the key does not include that chain. default_locale is an admin-changeable runtime setting; after it changes, locales that were missing the key keep serving the previous fallback language until the 300-entry cache evicts the entry. ensure_loaded! loading the new locale file does not invalidate those entries.

Negative queryset slices are invalid in Django

Django QuerySet slicing raises ValueError if start or stop is negative; it does not "handle negative slicing automatically" as the comment claims. A client-supplied cursor such as "0:-5:0" therefore 500s instead of paginating. The same false assumption was copied into BasePaginator.get_result (start_offset = offset when cursor.is_prev), so a negative prev offset now fails on every endpoint that uses BasePaginator, not only audit logs.

AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so the first page dies in build_cursor with TypeError, and any later cursor compares an int to a timestamp column in SQL. The endpoint should keep DateTimePaginator (or this class must use DateTimePaginator's multiplier and fromtimestamp conversion). As written, optimized_pagination=true always 500s for admins.

false_positives.candidate:
Eviction count is not atomic with the ZADD and can over-delete

Payloads are ZADDed in a separate pipeline, then each span runs this script, which ZPOPMINs down to 1000 using a count read inside the script. Two overlapping batches can each observe a count above 1000 and each pop span_count-1000 members, deleting more than the excess (including spans just inserted by the other batch). The cap is also a hardcoded 1000, while SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans (1001) is no longer enforced, and the segment_span_count_exceeded metric/log was removed, so drops are silent and not configurable.

No test covers insert-time eviction or zset merge

The buffer tests only add the new end_timestamp_precise field to existing small trees. Nothing asserts that a segment larger than 1000 spans ZPOPMINs the lowest scores, that the root span is kept, or that zunionstore still merges redirect keys. A WRONGTYPE against leftover SET keys and over-eviction across batches would not be caught.

Redirect walk limit cut from 10000 to 1000 splits deep segments

The parent-redirect loop now stops after 1000 hops instead of 10000 and still HSETs the span onto whatever set_span_id it reached. Traces whose redirect chain is deeper than 1000 are no longer joined to the real segment root; those spans are stored and flushed as a separate segment. The previous comment that this limit breaks joining was removed rather than the walk being fixed.

SET segment keys are incompatible with the new ZSET commands

process_spans now ZADDs span payloads and _load_segment_data ZSCANs them, while add-buffer.lua switched from SCARD/SUNIONSTORE to ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE/ZPOPMIN. Keys already written by the previous sadd/sunionstore path are Redis SETs. The first ZADD, ZUNIONSTORE, or ZSCAN on those keys returns WRONGTYPE, so in-flight segments cannot be merged or flushed and span ingestion fails until those keys expire. There is no new key prefix or migration.

Eligibility cache key uses process-local hash and is never invalidated

The check also ignores the query string actually executed: _get_event_stats passes the closed-over request into is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects, not the query argument. The code is therefore reusable under a race, contrary to the "exactly once" contract. Consume the code in a single conditional update (transaction or compare-and-swap on the encrypted blob) and only create the session if that update wins.

true_positives.matched_candidate:
Update/delete no longer fall back to a destination calendar

When `externalCalendarId` is missing, updateEvent and deleteEvent now do `destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`. That comparison is against a falsy id, so it never matches, and `calendarId` becomes undefined. Previously this fell back to `destinationCalendar.externalId`. Updates and deletes for bookings that have no stored external calendar id (or a null one) are sent to Google without a calendar id and fail, leaving stale events.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Organization slug assignment flag is inverted

This unrelated change flips `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` to `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}` while still writing `requestedSlug` only when billing is enabled. With billing off, the new organization is created with no slug, so its URL does not resolve. With billing on, slug is set immediately instead of only `requestedSlug`, skipping the billing gate the old condition enforced. Organization creation is broken in both configurations.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Lark still writes only the first destination calendar

createEvent, createAttendees, updateEvent, and deleteEvent all take `destinationCalendar[0].externalId` and ignore the credential CalendarManager now passes in. On a collective event that array starts with the organizer, so a co-host's Lark credential tries to create or delete on the organizer's calendar id and throws "no calendar id" or a permission error. The co-host never gets their own Lark event. Office 365 createEvent and the CalDAV base service have the same first-element-only behavior, so any non-Google host is not actually supported.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
updateEvent is called with an undefined credential

If a calendar reference has a credentialId that is not on the EventManager user and the DB lookup misses (or the credential has no app slug), `credential` stays undefined, but the code still pushes `updateEvent(credential, ...)`. getCalendar(undefined) throws, the surrounding catch returns failure for every reference, and remaining hosts' calendar events are not updated. createAllCalendarEvents guards this with `if (credential)`; the update path does not.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

false_positives.candidate:
Collective host calendars dropped when organizer has none

evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer user has a destination calendar, and the collective branch then does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. Optional chaining no-ops on null, so every co-host calendar collected above is discarded. Those hosts are not invited on their calendars even though they have destination calendars configured — the exact failure this PR describes — whenever the organizer has no destination calendar.

Organizer email is always the first destination calendar

createEvent (and updateEvent) set the Google organizer attendee email from `destinationCalendar[0]`, while the calendar written to is chosen by `credentialId`. For a collective booking EventManager calls createEvent once per host credential with the full destination array, so every host's event is created with the first host's calendar id as the organizer email. Secondary hosts can fail Google insert/update or get an event owned by the wrong identity, which is the case this PR is meant to fix.

Recurring cancel deletes the same event with every credential

The new loop walks every calendar booking reference, and the all-remaining recurring branch ignores that reference's credential. For each reference it loads every user calendar credential and, for each updated booking, deletes only the first `_calendar` reference (`find`) with that credential. One recurring series cancel therefore issues duplicate deletes of the same event id against unrelated calendars, and never targets the other hosts' references. Later instances can be left on calendars or the cancel promise set can fail.

Webhook destinationCalendar shape is now inconsistent

CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from a single object or null to an array, and handlers do not agree on the empty value: confirm/cancel send `[]`, while other payloads still emit `null` (the BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED webhook tests still expect null; only BOOKING_REJECTED was updated to []). Subscribers that read `payload.destinationCalendar.integration` or `externalId` will throw, and clients cannot rely on one type. The PR is marked non-breaking, but this is a webhook contract change.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing refresh_token is replaced with the literal string "refresh_token"

If the parsed token body has no `refresh_token`, this helper sets `data.refresh_token` to the string `"refresh_token"` and returns that object. Office 365's refresh schema treats `refresh_token` as optional because Microsoft often omits it and expects the client to keep the existing one; `Office365CalendarService` then spreads `tokenResponse.data` over the stored credential and saves it. The real refresh token is overwritten with the placeholder, so the next refresh fails and the Outlook connection is dead. The same placeholder is copied onto Zoom tokens whenever the sync parser is used.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync token schema cannot accept a real token response

When credential sync is enabled, refresh bodies are validated with `minimumTokenResponseSchema`. The computed keys `z.string().toString()` and `z.string().optional().toString()` are the literal property names of those Zod types (e.g. "ZodString"), not a catchall, and Zod objects strip unknown keys by default. A normal `{ access_token, expires_in }` body therefore fails validation and every synced refresh throws "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned". Even a passing parse would drop `expires_in`, so callers such as Zoom that do `Date.now() + expires_in * 1000` would store `NaN` and immediately treat the token as expired.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google refresh persists the Zod result and corrupts credentials

After every Google token refresh, the code assigns `key` to the return value of `parseRefreshTokenResponse` and writes that object to `credential.key`. That helper returns the Zod safeParse result (`{ success, data }`), not the credential payload. Previously this path stored `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`. The next calendar use calls `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` and fails, so a normal token refresh (syncing disabled) permanently breaks that user's Google Calendar connection until the app is reconnected.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync refresh returns a raw fetch Response that callers cannot use

When syncing is on, this helper returns the `fetch` Response and does not check `response.ok`, set `Content-Type`, or parse JSON. Callers were not updated to that shape: Google reads `res.data` (undefined on a Response, so the refresh throws and can mark the credential invalid), HubSpot treats the Response as a token and computes `expiryDate` from `expiresIn` (NaN) before `setAccessToken(undefined)`, and Zoho Bigin/Zoho CRM read `tokenInfo.data` as if it were an axios response. Lark still runs `handleLarkError` expecting a Lark envelope, but the comment says the sync endpoint returns only an access token and expiry. Token refresh for those apps fails as soon as `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, which is the documented test path.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync refresh returns a raw fetch Response that callers cannot use

When syncing is on, this helper returns the `fetch` Response and does not check `response.ok`, set `Content-Type`, or parse JSON. Callers were not updated to that shape: Google reads `res.data` (undefined on a Response, so the refresh throws and can mark the credential invalid), HubSpot treats the Response as a token and computes `expiryDate` from `expiresIn` (NaN) before `setAccessToken(undefined)`, and Zoho Bigin/Zoho CRM read `tokenInfo.data` as if it were an axios response. Lark still runs `handleLarkError` expecting a Lark envelope, but the comment says the sync endpoint returns only an access token and expiry. Token refresh for those apps fails as soon as `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set, which is the documented test path.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Zoho Bigin sync sends credential id as calcomUserId

`refreshAccessToken` calls `refreshOAuthTokens` with `credentialId` as the third argument. That argument is sent as `calcomUserId` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`. The parent app will look up the wrong user (or none) and return another user's tokens or an error, so Bigin refresh cannot succeed in sync mode. Other adapters correctly pass `credential.userId`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Salesforce client refresh calls prisma without importing it and keeps the old access token

`getClient` now always POSTs to `https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token` and then calls `prisma.credential.update`, but `prisma` is not imported in this file, so constructing a Salesforce calendar service throws ReferenceError before any event work. The new access token is also never passed into `jsforce.Connection` (`accessToken` stays `credentialKey.access_token`). This runs for every Salesforce credential, including when sync is disabled, and hardcoding `login.salesforce.com` fails sandbox and My Domain orgs that previously relied on the stored `instance_url`. It also never calls `refreshOAuthTokens`, so credential sync does not apply to Salesforce.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Credential webhook can duplicate or leave stale invalid credentials

The handler does `findFirst` by `userId` + `appId` and then create-or-update with no transaction and no `invalid: false`. Concurrent deliveries can both miss the row and insert two credentials; later reads use `findFirst` and ignore the other. An update of a credential already marked `invalid` keeps `invalid: true`, so synced tokens are never used. `schema.parse` and `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` are also uncaught, so a bad body or ciphertext becomes an unhandled 500 instead of 4xx, and there is no method check so non-POST requests are processed the same way.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

false_positives.candidate:
Zoom sync uses app slug zoomvideo instead of zoom

The refresh call passes `"zoomvideo"` as `appSlug`, but Zoom credentials are stored and addressed everywhere else as app id `"zoom"` (see the OAuth callback and the webhook's `appSlug` lookup). A self-hoster syncing by app slug will not find the Zoom credential and will refresh the wrong app or fail.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Guest dedupe and blacklist are case-sensitive

Existing attendees are excluded with guest === attendee.email, and BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased but the submitted guest is not. Mixed-case copies of an existing attendee are inserted again, and a blacklisted address can be added by changing letter case. Those addresses are then stored and included in calendar and email fan-out, including the meeting link.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Team admin/owner check requires both roles

isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner. A team admin who is not also the owner (and an owner who is not also an admin) is treated as unauthorized. Unless that user is the booking host or already an attendee, addGuests throws FORBIDDEN, so the people who manage team event types cannot add guests.

true_positives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Emails are keyed off the raw guest list, not the guests actually added

sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the original guests array after uniqueGuests has already dropped duplicates and blacklisted addresses. In sendAddGuestsEmails, any attendee whose email is in that raw list is sent AttendeeScheduledEmail (a new-booking confirmation) instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Re-submitting an existing attendee therefore sends them a fresh scheduling email and ICS REQUEST, while the database insert skipped them.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Add-guest emails ignore disableStandardEmails

sendAddGuestsEmails always emails the organizer, every team member, and every attendee. Sibling helpers (sendLocationChangeEmails, sendScheduledEmails, etc.) skip host or attendee mail when event type metadata sets disableStandardEmails. This path never receives that metadata, so event types that disabled standard mail still blast new-guest and full scheduled emails, including ICS attachments.

false_negatives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Attendees are committed before calendar/email, so a failed retry cannot finish the job

booking.update createMany runs before updateCalendarAttendees and sendAddGuestsEmails, with no transaction. If the calendar update throws, the mutation fails after the rows exist and emails never send. A retry then filters those emails out as already present, hits uniqueGuests.length === 0, and throws BAD_REQUEST, so the calendar and notifications stay permanently out of date.

Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, not the host's

updateCalendarAttendees is invoked with an EventManager built from ctx.user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). The mutation also allows attendees (and is intended to allow team admins) to add guests, and the booking query already loads the host's credentials but never uses them. When the caller is not the host, the organizer's destination calendar is updated with the wrong user's integrations, so the invite is not updated or a different calendar is written.

No checks for booking status, disableGuests, or seat capacity

Any organizer, attendee, or (broken) team admin can add an unbounded guest list to any booking id, including cancelled, rejected, and past bookings, and event types with guests disabled. Seated event types are not checked against seatsPerTimeSlot or BookingSeat; guests are inserted as normal attendees and then emailed the video URL. That bypasses event-type policy and can overfill seated events or leak meeting links from cancelled bookings.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
retryCount is a lost-update read-modify-write

Both failure paths set retryCount to the value loaded at the start of the loop (reminder.retryCount + 1) instead of an atomic increment. Overlapping cron runs that both read the same count and both fail write the same number back, so the counter can stay at 1 forever. Those reminders are never deleted by the retryCount > 1 cleanup and are rescheduled on every run until scheduledDate passes — the leak this PR is meant to stop. The same non-atomic update in the catch block is unguarded; if a concurrent run already deleted the row, Prisma throws and the exception leaves the for-loop, so the handler 500s and skips every remaining reminder in the batch.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
retryCount cleanup deletes every method, including already scheduled reminders

deleteMany's second OR branch matches only retryCount > 1 and does not constrain method to SMS or scheduled to false. WorkflowReminder is shared by EMAIL and WHATSAPP as well as SMS, and a row can be scheduled: true with a Twilio referenceId while still having retryCount > 1 (a later failed attempt only writes retryCount). The next cron run therefore permanently deletes those rows. Already-queued SMS can no longer be cancelled or reconciled, and any non-SMS reminder that ever exceeds one retry is removed even though this job is only supposed to drop failed SMS reminders.

false_positives.candidate:
Missing number or empty body never counts as a failed attempt

retryCount is only increased when scheduleSMS returns falsy or throws. If sendTo is missing or the rendered message is empty, the loop neither schedules nor increments and leaves scheduled false. The next cron selects the same row again, so those reminders are retried until scheduledDate is in the past. That is the same unbounded reschedule the PR describes, and it is not covered by the new retry limit.

No test for retry limit or the widened delete

The cron now deletes workflow reminders and gives up after two scheduling failures, but the PR adds no test for the retryCount > 1 predicate, the method/scheduled scope of that delete, or the increment on a falsy scheduleSMS result versus a missing sendTo. A wrong OR (as written) silently drops live reminders and would not be caught before merge.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

false_positives.candidate:
ANY() over JS arrays will fail at query time

Team and org authorization build `"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})` and `"userId" = ANY(${userIds})` by interpolating a JavaScript array into Prisma.sql (lines 164, 168, and 201). Prisma binds that array as one parameter; through the query engine it is not a Postgres integer array, so PostgreSQL rejects the predicate (`operator does not exist` / invalid array literal) when these conditions are executed. User-scope SQL does not use ANY, and the only `$queryRaw` test is user-scoped, so the suite never runs the broken statements. Use `IN (${Prisma.join(ids)})` or an explicit `ARRAY[${Prisma.join(ids)}]::int[]` cast, and execute team/org conditions against the database.

findMany removed; condition types changed to Prisma.Sql

InsightsBookingService no longer exposes findMany(BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs), and getAuthorizationConditions / getFilterConditions now return Prisma.Sql instead of BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedWhereInput. This PR only updates the service and its tests, so existing callers that pass a Prisma where/select into findMany, or that AND these conditions into a Prisma where object, will not compile and cannot query. Either keep a findMany wrapper that applies the SQL via $queryRaw, or update every caller in the same change.

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Empty updateMany will throw after writing calendar cache

fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache finishes by calling SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, {}). Prisma rejects updateMany when data has no fields ("data argument must have at least one field"), and @updatedAt is not applied unless an update actually runs. Every successful Google cache fill (webhook refresh and fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache) will therefore throw after the cache write, failing the caller and never bumping SelectedCalendar.updatedAt.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Webhook helper is macOS-only and writes the wrong env file

sed -i '' is BSD/macOS syntax and fails on GNU sed, so the script cannot update GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL on Linux. ENV_FILE is also ../.env relative to the current working directory, not apps/web/.env, so even a successful run does not update the env file Next.js actually loads and the tunnel URL is never used.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

false_positives.candidate:
Deleting cache does not refresh cache status in the UI

deleteCacheMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. Unlike the disconnect mutation in the same component, it never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars. The parent passes onChanged through but does not refetch that query, so after a successful delete the dropdown still shows the old "last updated" timestamp and "Delete cached data" until a full reload.

Migration stamps every existing cache row as updated now

updatedAt is added as NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), so every pre-existing CalendarCache row is recorded as updated at migration time rather than when it was actually written. The new cache-status UI uses max(updatedAt), so all current Google calendar caches will appear freshly updated even if they are old or near expiry. The SQL comment also still claims the column has no default, which is the opposite of what the statement does.

connectedCalendars query crashes when the user has no calendars

The handler always calls getCacheStatusByCredentialIds with connectedCalendars.map(cal => cal.credentialId). For a user with zero connected calendars that array is empty, and Prisma rejects credentialId: { in: [] } (empty IN lists are invalid). The connectedCalendars query, which this settings page loads with suspense, then errors instead of returning an empty list.

dev:cron now depends on tsx, which is not installed

The dev:cron script was changed from ts-node (a declared devDependency) to npx tsx, but tsx is not in package.json. yarn dev:cron will either fail or pull an unpinned tsx via npx, so the local cron tester no longer runs from the repo's locked dependencies.

true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Cancellation of workflow reminders is not awaited

On booking cancel, request-reschedule (bookings.tsx around the workflowReminders.forEach), workflow update, and reschedule (handleNewBooking.ts), deleteScheduledEmailReminder / deleteScheduledSMSReminder are started inside forEach and never awaited. This PR removed the previously awaited prisma.workflowReminder deletes, so the only record that a reminder must not be sent is the cancelled flag (or row delete) inside those async functions. Next.js ends the request when the handler promise resolves, which drops in-flight work. If that update or delete never commits, the cron still treats the reminder as active and SendGrid/Twilio still deliver the cancelled or rescheduled booking email or SMS.

true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
immediateDelete bypasses the cancelled flag and does not retry

deleteScheduledEmailReminder(..., immediateDelete=true) posts a SendGrid batch cancel and returns without setting cancelled or deleting the WorkflowReminder row. Reschedule (handleNewBooking), workflow delete, and step delete all pass true. That is the same immediate scheduled_sends cancel the PR says fails once 100 cancellations are pending, and a failure is only logged. Because cancelled stays false/null, scheduleEmailReminders will never retry the cancel, so those emails are still sent. On success the orphaned row also remains until scheduledDate passes.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

false_positives.candidate:
Cron still schedules reminders that were cancelled but not yet sent

After the cancel pass, unscheduled email reminders (scheduled=false, scheduledDate within 72 hours) are loaded with no filter on cancelled and no check that the booking is still ACCEPTED. Reminders that were never given a SendGrid referenceId are only removed by the un-awaited delete in deleteScheduledEmailReminder. If that delete does not commit, or a row is marked cancelled while still unscheduled, this loop creates a batch, sends the email, and sets scheduled=true. The scheduling query needs to exclude cancelled reminders and cancelled/rescheduled bookings before calling SendGrid.

One SendGrid cancel error aborts every pending cancellation

The cron loads every reminder with cancelled=true and scheduledDate within the next hour, then calls SendGrid and queues the row delete inside a single try around the whole loop. Deletes run only after every request succeeds. Any failure (null or stale referenceId, already-cancelled batch, rate limit) jumps to the catch, so no rows from that run are deleted and later reminders in the list are not cancelled. The next run hits the same already-cancelled or invalid batch first, throws again, and never reaches the rest. Those emails stay scheduled at SendGrid until send time, which is the original bug. Each reminder needs its own try/catch, a skip when referenceId is missing, and the row must be removed or left retryable even when SendGrid errors.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reschedule calendar/video cleanup is not awaited

getCalendar is now async, but the only call site wraps it in bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...). forEach does not wait for async callbacks, and the returned promises are discarded, so the try/catch around it never sees rejections from getCalendar or deleteEvent/deleteMeeting. Reschedule then sends the reschedule email and returns true while external calendar events and video meetings may still be deleting, or may fail as unhandled rejections and leave the old event on the calendar.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully

false_positives.candidate:
Cancel-all recurring events never waits on calendar deletes

When cancelling all remaining instances of a recurring booking, credentials are walked with .forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(...); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent) }). The callback is not awaited, and deletedEvent is the resolved value, not a promise, pushed only after deleteEvent finishes. Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)) later in the handler therefore runs before those pushes, so recurring calendar events are not reliably deleted and errors are not surfaced to the cancel request. The non-recurring branch just below was correctly converted to for...of; this branch was not.

Dynamic imports still load every app immediately

Each app is stored as import("./...") in an object literal, so every promise starts as soon as this module is evaluated. Any importer of appStore (calendar, video, payment, bookings) therefore kicks off a load of every integration at once. That does not defer unused apps, and it replaces one static graph with many parallel chunks that all start together, which can make cold starts slower rather than lazy.

Wipe-my-cal reschedule cleanup is not awaited

Same as the vital reschedule path: bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...) awaits getCalendar only inside a callback that nothing awaits. Calendar deleteEvent and video deleteMeeting are not part of the function's control flow, the surrounding try/catch cannot handle their failures, and the handler can finish (and email the user) before those integrations are actually torn down.

requestReschedule does not wait for integration deletes

requestReschedule now awaits getCalendar inside bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async ...), which does not await the callback. deleteEvent/deleteMeeting promises are dropped, so the mutation proceeds to send the reschedule email and BOOKING_CANCELLED webhooks without knowing whether the old calendar event or video meeting was removed. true_positives.golden_comment: Incorrect end time calculation using slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
true_positives.matched_candidate:

The new working-hours gate uses slot start minutes for both start and end, so a slot that begins inside hours but runs past endTime is not detected. It also uses Array.find and treats the first same-day range that does not contain the slot as 'outside hours'. A host with two ranges on one day (for example 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00) will fail the check for almost every slot, because each slot misses at least one range. Those slots are then removed for every fixed host, which can make an otherwise bookable round-robin event show no availability. Days with no working-hour entry are not rejected at all, so a fixed host can still be offered on days they do not work.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using === for dayjs object comparison will always return false as it compares object references, not values. Use .isSame() method instead: dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, 'minutes').isSame(dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, minutes))
true_positives.matched_candidate:
All-day blocked overrides never match

A zero-length date override (start equal to end) is the usual way an organizer marks a day unavailable. The check compares two separately constructed dayjs objects with ===, which is reference equality and is always false, so that branch never runs. Combined with the early return when dateOverrideExist is set, a blocked day is treated as fully available instead of closed, and busy times on that day are also skipped.

false_positives.candidate:
New test does not cover either bug the PR claims to fix

The only added assertion re-requests the same personal-event override in Asia/Dhaka and expects the identical UTC slot list. It never builds a round-robin event with a fixed host, never asserts that slots outside the fixed host's override disappear, and never checks that an override moves to a different invitee-local calendar day. A regression in checkIfIsAvailable or in the midnight-crossing offset math would still pass CI.

Override date match mixes server-local and UTC formatting

slotStartTime is a UTC dayjs, but the override side is dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset).format(...), which formats in the server's local timezone, not UTC or the organizer zone. The offset itself is also applied to an absolute instant and then compared with UTC slot instants. On any host whose TZ is not UTC, or when the organizer offset moves the override across midnight, the same-day test and the isBefore/isAfter window checks attach the override to the wrong day or the wrong clock times, so fixed-host overrides still do not constrain the slots the PR is trying to fix.

Override days skip busy checks and can double-book

In checkIfIsAvailable, once any date override falls on the same calendar day as the slot, dateOverrideExist is set and the function returns true as soon as the slot is not rejected as outside that override. That return happens before the busy-interval loop. Fixed hosts and round-robin hosts therefore look free for every slot inside an override window even when they already have a Cal booking or calendar conflict covering that time, so the booking page will offer times that cannot actually be taken.

Timezone-adjusted overrides lose the day when they cross midnight

Override start and end are shifted by inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset and then reduced to hour() and minute() only. If the shift crosses midnight, hour() wraps to the other side of the day (for example 01:00 minus a 10h offset becomes 15:00) and the previous/next day is discarded. buildSlots then places that window on the invitee's current day. Attendees in a timezone far from the organizer see the override on the wrong date, or miss it, which is the timezone bug this change is meant to fix whenever the adjusted range is not on the same calendar day.

false_positives.candidate:
Graceful shutdown does not drain queued work before stopping commits

OrderedQueueWorker.run checks self.shutdown at the top of the loop, and FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets that flag before waking the workers. A worker that finishes the current item, or that is unblocked from get() with items still queued, exits without processing the rest of the queue. close() also stops and joins the commit thread before pool.shutdown(), so anything completed after the last commit iteration is never committed by this strategy, and anything still queued is abandoned. Arroyo's join contract is that submitted messages are finished or the timeout fires; here in-flight uptime results are dropped on the floor until a later replay, and a replay will not happen for any offset the commit thread already advanced past.

Offsets are committed from a background thread

_commit_loop runs on a daemon thread started in SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy and calls the Arroyo commit callback directly. That callback commits through the Kafka consumer, which the processor is also using on the main thread for poll, assignment, and close. librdkafka consumers are not thread-safe; concurrent commit and poll/close can crash the consumer or corrupt the group offset. Commits need to be handed back to the processing thread (for example recorded in poll() and committed there).

Queue stats test can pass or fail depending on worker timing

test_stats_reporting submits 10 items and immediately asserts get_stats()['total_items'] > 0. Workers are already running, so a fast result_processor can drain every queue before that assertion. The same file's test_different_groups_distributed asserts that 20 hashed keys always land on all 3 queues, which hash() does not guarantee. Both tests will flake under load or a different PYTHONHASHSEED.

Queues are unbounded, so submit never applies backpressure

Each work queue is queue.Queue() with no maxsize, and FixedQueuePool.submit always put()s without blocking. The class docstring claims natural backpressure when queues fill, but the Arroyo consumer thread can keep polling and enqueueing forever while workers lag. A slow subscription (the case this mode is meant to isolate) or a dead worker grows memory without bound and can OOM the process. submit() needs a bounded queue and must block (or otherwise stall the consumer) when that queue is full.

Rebalance shuts down the shared pool, then failed submits are committed

FixedQueuePool is created once on ResultsStrategyFactory and reused by every SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy from create_with_partitions. Strategy.close/terminate (and factory.shutdown) call queue_pool.shutdown(), which shuts the queues and joins the workers. On the next assignment Arroyo builds a new strategy against that same dead pool. submit() then fails on Queue.put (queue.ShutDown), and the except Exception handler add_offset+complete_offset's the message. The new strategy's commit thread treats that as committable and commits offset+1. Those results are acknowledged and never processed, so uptime checks are dropped after the first revoke/rebalance or any close().

Shutdown joins every worker for 5s and join() drops the timeout

FixedQueuePool.shutdown sets worker.shutdown then queue.shutdown, then joins each worker with timeout=5.0 in series. A worker blocked in result_processor (DB/HTTP) does not notice shutdown until the current item finishes, so N queues can block shutdown for about N*5 seconds (100s at the default 20). SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.join ignores the timeout Arroyo passes and always calls close(), which also joins the commit thread for another 5s before shutting the pool. A revoke or process shutdown can therefore exceed the Kafka session/max.poll interval and trigger another rebalance while workers are still running. join() must honor its timeout, and worker joins need a single shared deadline.
